author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Novartis shareholders are placing fresh scrutiny on the drugmaker’s acquisition strategy after two clinical setbacks in quick succession raised questions about the value and execution of its pipeline, Reuters reported Friday.

The latest disappointment came when the late-stage study of del-desiran failed, following another setback days earlier. The events renewed investor attention on Novartis’s roughly $12 billion purchase of Avidity Biosciences and on whether recent dealmaking will produce enough successful medicines to support growth.

Novartis shares recorded an 11% one-day decline after the news, wiping out nearly $30 billion in market value and erasing their gains for the year, according to Reuters. That was a reported market move, not a live price.

Chief Executive Vas Narasimhan has committed more than $30 billion to acquisitions and partnerships over the past three years. Some investors still expressed confidence in the broader pipeline, but the failures increase pressure for clear trial milestones and disciplined spending. Drug development is inherently uncertain, making portfolio breadth and the price paid for experimental assets central to how markets judge pharmaceutical strategy.
dek: A failed late-stage trial and another recent disappointment are intensifying questions about the drugmaker’s acquisitions and pipeline execution.
headline: Novartis investors scrutinize deal strategy after clinical setbacks
